newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian SGB mulls Elf, Suez sales.
newsitem.headline: Belgian SGB mulls Elf, Suez sales.

text.p: Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA reiterated on Thursday it was studying selling its minority stakes in French parent Cie. de Suez and French oil group Elf Aquitaine.
"Our strategy is to sell our stakes in Elf and Suez, but we are waiting. We will do it when the market conditions are right," SGB spokesman Guy Dellicour told Reuters.
SGB owns 1.40 percent of Suez, which itself owns 63 percent of SGB, and 1.33 percent of Elf.
It first made its intention to sell the stakes known earlier this year.

SGB chairman Etienne Davignon said in April the Elf stake could be put up for sale because an obligation to hold the stake, acquired from the French government at the time of Elf's privatization, ended earlier this year.
Davignon noted at the time that the sale of the Elf stake then would have led to a small capital loss for SGB.
Dellicour declined to comment if SGB believed market conditions had now improved.
There has been much speculation how SGB, which this week announced it would pay 49 billion Belgian francs to boost its stake in utility holding Tractebel SA, will raise new funds.
Announcing the deal on Tuesday, SGB said it would raise most of the money from newly agreed credit lines but did not provide details.
